payload.text:
I'd hold access-roles back from main for now. The admin gate has a real bug. I didn't change anything; I only read the diff and tested copies of the files outside the repo.

**Blocker: `access/gate.py`, line 4**
```python
return role is 'admin'
```
This checks whether the role is the exact same object in memory, not whether it says "admin". Your own README and `docs/roles.md` say never to compare roles this way. When a role is built at runtime, like `role_from_config(' Admin ')`, it reads as `'admin'` but is a separate object. I ran that case and the gate returned **False**, so a real admin whose role comes from config gets locked out of the admin tools.

The fault isn't always a lockout, either. The result depends on string interning, which can change between Python versions and builds, so the gate doesn't behave reliably. Python also flags this line (`SyntaxWarning: "is" with a literal`), and with warnings treated as errors the module fails to import at all.

**Fix:** `return role == 'admin'`

**Why the tests didn't catch it:** `test_gate.py` only uses the literal `'admin'`, which happens to be the same object, so the test passes. Please add a test with a role built at runtime, for example `has_access({'role': role_from_config(' ADMIN ')}, 'admin-tools')` should be True. A `'team-' + x` case would also help.

**Smaller points (not blockers):**
- A user with no role returns False, which is the right default. A test for that would lock it in.
- `team.py` and `config.py` look fine. `is_team_role` will crash if the role is `None`, so check that callers always pass a string.
- Every tool other than `admin-tools` is open to everyone, as the README says. If you add more admin-only tools later, an allowlist would be safer than this one-off check.
- The version bump, CHANGES and docs are all consistent.

Once the `==` fix and a runtime-role test are in, I'm happy for this to merge.
